Test Case Name: Compare Navigation Bar Layout with AngularJS
Preconditions: Original AngularJS navigation bar accessible, Vue 3 navigation rendered
Test Steps:
1. Take screenshot of AngularJS navigation bar (desktop)
2. Take screenshot of Vue 3 navigation bar (desktop)
3. Compare both screenshots pixel by pixel
Expected Results:
- Navigation bar height matches (±2px tolerance)
- Font family, size, weight are identical
- Colors (background, text, hover) are identical
- Spacing and padding match
- Overall appearance is indistinguishable

Test Steps:
1. Observe navigation bar position
2. Scroll down the page
3. Check if navigation bar behavior matches AngularJS
Expected Results:
- Navigation bar positioned at top
- Positioning behavior (fixed/static/sticky) matches AngularJS
- Z-index appropriate (appears above content)

Test Steps:
1. Observe default link styling
2. Hover over each link
3. Click a link and observe active state
4. Navigate to different pages and observe active indicator
Expected Results:
- Default state matches AngularJS styling
- Hover state matches AngularJS hover effect
- Active state: current page link visually distinguished
- Focus state: keyboard focus indicator matches AngularJS

Test Steps:
1. Check if navigation links have icons
2. Compare icon display with AngularJS version
3. Verify icon alignment and sizing
Expected Results:
- If AngularJS has icons, Vue 3 displays identical icons
- Icons properly aligned with text
- Icon size and spacing match original

Test Steps:
1. Load the application
2. Observe navigation bar layout
3. Compare with AngularJS at same resolution
Expected Results:
- All 10 links displayed horizontally
- No overflow or wrapping
- Layout matches AngularJS exactly
- All links easily clickable

Test Steps:
1. Resize browser to 1366x768px
2. Observe navigation bar layout
3. Compare with AngularJS at same resolution
Expected Results:
- Navigation bar adapts appropriately
- All links remain accessible
- Behavior matches AngularJS (horizontal or hamburger menu)

Test Steps:
1. Resize browser to tablet dimensions
2. Observe navigation bar transformation
3. Test interaction with navigation
4. Compare with AngularJS
Expected Results:
- Navigation bar matches AngularJS responsive behavior
- If hamburger menu, all 10 links accessible
- Touch targets appropriately sized (44x44px min)
- Menu opens/closes smoothly

Test Steps:
1. Resize browser to mobile dimensions
2. Observe navigation bar transformation
3. Test hamburger menu
4. Verify all links accessible
5. Compare with AngularJS
Expected Results:
- Navigation bar matches AngularJS mobile behavior
- Hamburger menu icon visible and functional
- Tapping hamburger opens full menu
- All 10 links accessible
- Menu easily scrollable
- Touch targets appropriately sized

Test Steps:
1. Rotate device to landscape or resize browser
2. Observe navigation bar layout
3. Test navigation functionality
4. Compare with AngularJS
Expected Results:
- Navigation adapts to landscape
- Behavior matches AngularJS
- All links accessible
- Layout uses horizontal space efficiently

Test Steps:
1. Load application on ultra-wide screen
2. Observe navigation bar layout
3. Compare with AngularJS
Expected Results:
- Navigation bar scales appropriately
- Links not awkwardly spaced
- Layout matches AngularJS behavior

Test Steps:
1. Press Tab to navigate through links
2. Verify tab order (left to right)
3. Press Enter on each link to navigate
4. Use Shift+Tab to navigate backwards
Expected Results:
- All 10 links keyboard accessible
- Tab order logical: Search → Events → Attendees → Websites → Surveys → Email messages → Mailing list → Users → Accounts → Contacts DB → Prospects
- Focused link has visible focus indicator
- Enter triggers navigation
- Matches AngularJS keyboard behavior

Test Steps:
1. Enable screen reader
2. Navigate to navigation bar
3. Tab through all links
4. Listen to screen reader announcements
Expected Results:
- Navigation bar announced as landmark
- Each link label clearly announced
- Current active page identified
- Experience matches AngularJS
- ARIA labels/roles properly implemented

Test Steps:
1. Inspect navigation bar HTML
2. Verify ARIA attributes present
3. Validate against WCAG 2.1 AA
Expected Results:
- <nav> element or role='navigation' present
- Current page link has aria-current='page'
- Links have appropriate aria-label if needed
- ARIA attributes match AngularJS

Test Steps:
1. Use color contrast analyzer tool
2. Check contrast ratio for all text colors
3. Test default, hover, active states
Expected Results:
- All text has minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio (WCAG AA)
- Contrast ratios match or exceed AngularJS
- Hover states maintain sufficient contrast

Test Steps:
1. Click a navigation link
2. Observe where focus is placed after navigation
3. Compare with AngularJS behavior
Expected Results:
- Focus managed appropriately after navigation
- Focus moves to main content or stays as per AngularJS
- No focus traps
- Skip links function correctly (if present)

Test Steps:
1. Clear cache and reload page
2. Measure time from page load to navigation fully rendered
3. Compare with AngularJS
Expected Results:
- Navigation bar renders within 500ms
- Performance equal to or better than AngularJS
- No layout shift (CLS) during render

Test Steps:
1. Click each navigation link
2. Measure time to route change and page render
3. Record any lag or delays
Expected Results:
- Click response immediate (<100ms)
- Route changes occur smoothly
- No perceived lag vs AngularJS

Test Steps:
1. Navigate through all 10 sections multiple times
2. Monitor memory usage
3. Check for memory leaks
Expected Results:
- No memory leaks detected
- Memory usage stable
- Performance equal to or better than AngularJS

Test Steps:
1. Click on 'Events' link
2. Click on 'Users' link
3. Click on 'Search' link
4. Navigate back using browser back button
5. Navigate forward using browser forward button
Expected Results:
- Navigation bar remains visible and functional on all pages
- Active link indicator updates correctly
- Browser back/forward buttons work correctly
- State maintained appropriately

2. Observe application behavior
Expected Results:

Test Steps:

3. Observe loading behavior
